title: How Reliable Are Explanations of Language Models That Detect Insider Threats?
abstract: arXiv:2611.25796v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Organizations monitor their workers' activity for insider threats, in which workers misuse their legitimate access, by copying confidential files before leaving. Detectors score how unusual each day of activity is, flagging the most unusual for an analyst to review. Prominent current approaches use opaque neural networks, so explanations of a flag point to internal features: patterns of neuron activity most active on days of misuse. We audit such explanations for language-model detectors trained on CERT's simulated workplace logs. To test an explanation, we see what happens to the detector's score when we remove its features inside the model. We compare this to a control: a change that is as similar as possible to the removal, but without actually removing the features. translated_title: 检测内部威胁的语言模型解释有多可靠？
translated_abstract: 组织机构会监测员工的活动以防范内部威胁，即员工滥用其合法访问权限的行为，例如在离职前复制机密文件。检测器会对员工每天活动的异常程度进行评分，并将最异常的情况标记出来供分析师审查。当前主流方法使用不透明的神经网络，因此对某个标记的解释指向模型的内部特征：即在滥用行为发生的日子里最活跃的神经元活动模式。我们对在CERT模拟工作场所日志上训练的语言模型检测器的此类解释进行了审计。为了检验某个解释，我们观察当在模型内部移除其特征时检测器分数会发生什么变化，并将其与一个对照组进行比较：该变化尽可能类似于移除操作，但实际上并未移除这些特征。由于定义“相似”需要选择一种度量方式，我们的核心贡献是“倾覆半径”：即对该度量必须移动多远之后结论才会发生改变的一阶预测。
tldr: 本文提出“倾覆半径”这一核心贡献，通过一阶预测度量特征移除的相似对照变化何时会颠覆检测器的结论，从而审计内部威胁检测语言模型解释的可靠性。
en_tdlr: This paper's central contribution is the "tipping radius," a first-order prediction of how far a chosen similarity metric must move before removing a model's internal features changes the detector's conclusion, used to audit the reliability of explanations from language models that detect insider threats.
